definitions.meaning: the outer, thinner bone of the lower leg
a Roman clasp or pin for fastening a cloak

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for a clasp was borrowed by anatomists for the slender leg bone, so one word covers both senses.

parts.note: the season between summer and winter (American autumn) appears brief, and the phrase also means to be not enough

explanation.surface: A question whether autumn feels too brief.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans call autumn the fall, the season between summer and winter; if it seems short, the phrase is an idiom for being inadequate.
explanation.definitionFit: To come up short of a target or standard is to be inadequate.

parts.note: a sporting victory party, reread as the blaze that follows striking a match

explanation.surface: Fans celebrate outdoors after a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests a football game; it is the matchstick that lights the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A large outdoor fire is lit for festivities, and starts with a struck match.

clue.text: Non-U work a conservative chemist does here?

parts.note: labor is the American spelling of labour; Non-U means not upper-class British usage
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Unrefined work is what a Tory chemist gets on with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-U' (not upper-class) is Nancy Mitford's term for vulgar usage; here it signals the un-British spelling. The definition reads 'where a chemist does (work)'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist conducts experiments in a lab.

parts.note: a line from the nursery rhyme about an executioner's axe, reread as the place where a helicopter (a chopper) arrives

explanation.surface: A quotation from the old London bells rhyme that ends with an executioner's axe.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'Oranges and Lemons' ends 'here comes a chopper to chop off your head'; read literally, 'here' is a landing place and the chopper a helicopter.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing pad for helicopters is exactly where a chopper comes in.

indicators.note: wrecked means smashed up, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A railway saboteur derails an eastern-line train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' and 'train' paint a rail crash; 'train' is a retinue.
explanation.definitionFit: A train in this sense is the retinue following an important person.

clue.text: Bit of news causes some excitement

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A news story stirs up a little interest.
explanation.definitionFit: A single news report or story is called an item.

definitions.meaning: a name for several marine fish, such as the long-tailed duck-fish
Joan of 'Darby and Joan', the devoted elderly married couple

explanation.definitionFit: It is a name for various marine fish, and Joan, in the old pair Darby and Joan, is an aged spouse.

clue.text: "Ask where's the North? at York, 'tis on the ——" (Pope)

definitions.text: "Ask where's the North? at York, 'tis on the ——" (Pope)

parts.words: Ask where's the North? at York, 'tis on the
parts.note: a quotation from Pope's Essay on Man, the missing word being the river at the Scottish border

explanation.surface: A line of Pope about how everyone puts the North further away.
explanation.walkthrough: Pope's point: ask a Yorkshireman where the North is and he says it lies further on, at the border river.
explanation.definitionFit: The river forms part of the boundary between England and Scotland.

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: paws is a jokey word for hands

explanation.surface: A show of hands to agree a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange one thing for another is to trade.

parts.note: extended means long
a bow is a gesture of courtesy

explanation.surface: Archers display a drawn-out bit of politeness.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is ARCHERS, so the definition is a weapon such people use.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall English war bow was the archer's classic weapon.

clue.text: Revolutionary agent finds injured lad in tree

indicators.note: the injured words are knocked out of shape, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy is found hurt up a tree after a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary agent' suggests a rebel spy; it is a foot pedal that makes a wheel go round. 'injured' rearranges LAD and TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot pedal drives the wheel of a sewing machine or lathe round, so it is the agent of rotation.

clue.text: Change the small pair, Curtis up. One for the road

indicators.note: the instruction to change these letters signals they are rearranged

parts.note: PR is the short form of pair

explanation.surface: Instructions to swap a small pair of things around, with someone called Curtis getting up.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell drink offered to a rider already mounted is a parting drink, the original one for the road.

indicators.note: sounding means the word is judged by how it is said

parts.note: kid as an adjective means young, as in a kid brother

explanation.surface: A pirate captain who seems young.
explanation.walkthrough: William Kidd was a notorious seventeenth-century Scottish privateer turned pirate; his name is said just like 'kid'.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain William Kidd was hanged for piracy in 1701.

parts.note: a score is written music
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A recorder player's sheet music rests on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recorder' looks like the instrument; it is the thing that records a game's points. 'on' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: The board at a ground keeps a record of points in a game.

clue.text: Excel in attack from the trenches

definitions.meaning: to excel is to rise higher than, surpass
soldiers going over the top climbed out of the trench to attack

explanation.definitionFit: To surpass is to rise above others; and in First World War slang, going over the top was leaving the trench to charge.

clue.text: Punctuality was that of Louis XVIII

definitions.text: Punctuality was that of Louis XVIII

parts.words: Punctuality was that of Louis XVIII
parts.note: Louis XVIII is credited with saying punctuality is the courtesy of kings

explanation.surface: A historical remark about a French king's timekeeping.
explanation.walkthrough: The French saying 'l'exactitude est la politesse des rois' is attributed to Louis XVIII.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtesy or good manners, in the French word used in the king's maxim.

clue.text: Family all set to take a bow?

definitions.meaning: the Archer family of the long-running BBC radio soap

definitions.text: all set to take a bow?
definitions.meaning: people ready to pick up a bow and shoot

explanation.definitionFit: The Archers is a BBC radio serial about a farming family, and bowmen are those who take up bows.

indicators.note: obscurely means the words are muddled, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A cryptic murmur about seeing things dimly.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of something is to see it.

clue.text: Sound quality many found in this instrument

parts.note: timbre is the tone quality of a sound
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so many

explanation.surface: A musician admires the rich tone heard from a particular instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' only links; L comes after the sound quality, not inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A timbrel is an old tambourine-like hand drum mentioned in the Bible.

clue.text: The mace converted into a cutting weapon

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ceremonial club is reworked into a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad heavy jungle knife is used both as a tool and a blade.

parts.note: ears are the organs we listen with
red means hot, as in red-hot

explanation.surface: Communist eavesdroppers are moved close enough to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red listeners' tempts with Soviet spies; it is burning ears, which are said to glow when people talk about you.
explanation.definitionFit: The distance at which a sound can be heard is a range of hearing.

clue.text: Courage, when foreign kings invade the border

indicators.note: invade means one piece goes into another

parts.note: a hem is the border of a garment
rois is French for kings

explanation.surface: Bravery is needed when foreign monarchs cross the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' is a frontier in the surface but a hem of cloth in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravery and valour are the qualities of heroes.

clue.text: Shrub which in the east produces a drug

definitions.text: Shrub which in the east produces a drug

parts.words: Shrub which in the east produces a drug
parts.note: a description of the plant whose leaves give ..., grown in the eastern Andes

explanation.surface: A botanical note on a plant yielding a narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American bush's leaves are the source of cocaine.

definitions.meaning: an orange butterfly with a white mark on its underside

explanation.definitionFit: It is a punctuation mark, and also a European butterfly named for the white C-shaped mark on its wing.

parts.note: a fruit plant whose leaves stand for rank, read beside rank meaning foul-smelling

explanation.surface: A fruit whose foliage smells bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' suggests a bad smell; it means nobility: the leaves of this plant decorate a duke's coronet.
explanation.definitionFit: Its leaves are the emblem on ducal and marquess coronets, so the strawberry leaves signify high rank.

indicators.note: returns means the letters are taken back the other way

parts.note: the first four letters of 24 across, the fruit

explanation.surface: A university department comes back first.
explanation.definitionFit: A university division covering humanities is commonly called this.
An odd character is called this, and a joker is also a playing card and a wag.

clue.text: Girls going wild, hearing wretched publicity

indicators.note: hearing tells us the words count by how they are said

parts.note: wretched means mean and publicity means ads, giving mean ads

explanation.surface: Young women run riot after hearing some dreadful press coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: These were the frenzied female followers of Bacchus, women in a wild ecstasy.

clue.text: Does flattery get them to a date in Rome?

parts.note: dies is the Latin word for a day

explanation.surface: Asking whether compliments win you an evening out in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'date' suggests a romantic outing; in Rome (Latin) it is the word for day.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycophants are the ones who win favour by flattering.

clue.text: Where Argus follows with the herd

definitions.text: Where Argus follows with the herd

parts.words: Where Argus follows with the herd
parts.note: a place-name that comes before the name of a breed of cattle

explanation.surface: Where the hundred-eyed herdsman of myth trails his cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Argus', but the setter surely meant 'Angus': Aberdeen Angus is a Scottish breed of beef cattle, so the place comes before Angus in the herd's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish city gives its name to the black beef breed, with the county name following it.

definitions.meaning: a man hired for odd jobs
in tossing coins, the one whose coin differs is the ... out and is eliminated

explanation.definitionFit: An odd-job man does occasional work; and a coin toss leaves one player out when his result differs from the rest.
